evidence.description: The selected endpoint is force-unwrapped when constructing the network configuration.

candidates.explanation: The selected endpoint is optional, but it is used without checking whether it exists. If the selected URL provider endpoint is nil, constructing the tracker traps instead of handling the missing configuration.
candidates.title: Force-unwrapped analytics endpoint

evidence.description: Initialization explicitly configures six autotracking properties after creating the tracker.
Updating the tracker assigns the factory result without applying the initialization-time autotracking settings.
Reset also assigns the factory result without applying those settings.
The shared factory does not contain the explicit autotracking assignments performed by the initializer.

candidates.explanation: The initial tracker receives explicit autotracking settings, while the reset and update paths omit that configuration step. Those paths therefore depend on factory or SDK defaults rather than consistently establishing the same tracking configuration.
candidates.title: Tracker configuration differs across creation paths

evidence.description: The normal tracking path excludes the SDK tracking call when TESTING is defined.
The usage-data setting method calls the SDK directly without the TESTING condition.

candidates.explanation: Although ordinary event submission is disabled under TESTING, sendAnonymousUsageDataSetting still invokes tracker.track in those builds. Its direct call bypasses test-build suppression as well as the explicitly intended consent check bypass, leaving this event eligible for submission during testing.
candidates.title: Direct tracking bypasses test-build suppression
